question: Should OpenClaw expose Discord bot presence mutation to plugins as a public runtime API, and what gate, account scoping, and precedence model should it use?
rationale: The internal gateway capability exists, but promoting it to plugin runtime changes the public plugin contract and exposes a Discord bot-credential-backed mutation boundary to plugin code.

options.title: Design a gated runtime API
options.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence` runtime seam with explicit authorization, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence with static and auto presence.

options.title: Keep current surfaces only
options.body: Leave dynamic presence mutation on static config, auto-presence, and the default-off `setPresence` message action instead of giving plugins direct runtime control.

options.title: Fold into self-profile direction
options.body: Defer this request behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/34004 if maintainers want one Discord identity/profile API instead of a presence-only plugin API.

recommendation.title: Design a gated runtime API
recommendation.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence` runtime seam with explicit authorization, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence with static and auto presence.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a public plugin-runtime API and security-boundary decision, while Discord-specific implementation input should come from the Discord presence owners.
